candidate.answerReason: The centroid divides each median in a 2:1 ratio. The perpendicular median segments give area BGC = 64/3, which is one third of the whole triangle's area.

methods.label: Use the centroid and compare areas
methods.explanation:
The perpendicular medians create a right triangle whose area we can calculate directly. Let \(G\) be their intersection, as labeled in the figure. The centroid divides each median in the ratio \(2:1\), measured from the vertex, so
\[
BG=\frac23(8)=\frac{16}{3},\qquad CG=\frac23(12)=8.
\]
Because \(BG\perp CG\),
\[
[ BGC ]=\frac12\cdot\frac{16}{3}\cdot8=\frac{64}{3},
\]
where brackets denote area.

To relate this to the whole triangle, triangles \(BGC\) and \(BDC\) have bases on the same line \(BD\) and share the altitude from \(C\). Their area ratio is therefore \(BG:BD=2:3\). Also, \(BD\) is a median, so triangle \(BDC\) has half the area of triangle \(ABC\). Consequently,
\[
[ BGC ]=\frac23\cdot\frac12[ ABC ]=\frac13[ ABC ].
\]
Thus \([ ABC ]=3\cdot\frac{64}{3}=\boxed{64}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
